conceptual assets.information: The payload written through the CSR data path and queued for transmission over the ICC interface. The IP depends on it to deliver outgoing inter-CPU communication data.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The payload can be exposed at the ICC data output through the FIFO connection at lines 81 and 86. CSR writes can change the queued payload through the write-enable decode at line 60 and the FIFO input at line 81. FIFO enqueue and dequeue control can withhold or lose delivery through lines 60, 82, and 85-87. No privileged, override, bypass, or test behavior is shown.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could observe the ICC data output, inject a different CSR write, or prevent FIFO progress so that transmitted data is disclosed, corrupted, or withheld.

conceptual assets.information: The data received on the ICC interface and returned through the CSR read-data path. Software depends on it to consume incoming inter-CPU communication data.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The received payload is exposed through csr_rdata_o at line 52. The read process can return zero instead of the payload or select whether it is returned using lines 45 and 51-53. The same ready and address conditions can withhold the payload from the CSR interface at lines 46-53. No privileged, override, bypass, or test behavior is shown.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could read the CSR response, manipulate the read-selection or ready conditions, or suppress the read so that received data is exposed, altered, or unavailable.

conceptual assets.information: The CSR read request and address selection that request the received-data register view. The IP depends on this command to select and return the incoming communication payload.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Changing csr_re_i or csr_addr_i changes which read operation is recognized and which value is returned, as shown at lines 46-55. The same request and address conditions can prevent the receive-data response or its acknowledgement through lines 46-59. No privileged, override, bypass, or test behavior is shown.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could alter the CSR read request or address so that software receives the wrong value or the receive-data access is not serviced.

conceptual assets.information: The FIFO-generated indication that transmitted data is available to the ICC peer. The peer depends on it to determine whether outgoing communication can proceed.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The FIFO produces the indication on the ICC ready field at line 87, and FIFO write and read activity can change that indication through lines 82 and 85. A false unavailable indication can block the peer from accepting outgoing data, while a false available indication can cause incorrect transfer behavior at line 87. No privileged, override, bypass, or test behavior is shown.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could cause the FIFO availability indication to be asserted or suppressed incorrectly, making the ICC peer accept invalid timing or stop accepting transmitted data.

conceptual assets.information: The acknowledgement event generated for a CSR read of the ICC data address. The communication interface depends on it to signal completion of that operation.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The acknowledgement value is produced from the CSR read request and address comparison at line 59, so an incorrect value can misrepresent completion to the ICC peer. Suppressing or falsely asserting the acknowledgement can block or incorrectly advance the associated communication operation at line 59. No privileged, override, bypass, or test behavior is shown.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could cause the acknowledgement to be withheld or asserted for the wrong CSR access, stalling the communication operation or making the peer treat an incomplete operation as complete.

considered, not kept.concept: Transmit FIFO push/pop controls and free status

considered, not kept.reason: Clock and reset inputs and their instance connections are explicitly excluded from conceptual assets by the clock and reset rule.
FIFO depth, width, synchronization, safety, and reset options are fixed generics at lines 67-71 and cannot be changed or withheld at run time.
